title: Telling sound-alike words apart with pictures
examples: How do I know when to write see or sea?
What is the difference between write and right?

points: Two e letters, like two eyes

right.title: sea
points: Has an e and an a

explain.say: Some words sound exactly the same but mean different things. They are called homophones, which means same sound. Look at see and sea on the board. Listen: they sound the same!

faq.a: A homophone is a word that sounds the same as another word but means something different, and is often spelled differently, like see and sea.
See has two e letters, like two eyes. You see with your eyes.
Sea has an e and an a. Picture a wave over the a, because the sea is big, salty water.

faq.q: How do I know which one to write?
faq.a: Think about the meaning first, then picture it. Is it about eyes or water? A pencil or your hand? The picture picks the spelling.
There are lots: two and too, hear and here, night and knight, pair and pear. A teacher or grown-up can help you make a picture card for each pair.

facts: The word homophone comes from Greek words meaning same sound.
See and sea are homophones: they sound the same but mean different things.

quiz.say: Fish swim in the blank. Which word fits?
quiz.why: Sea is the big, salty water where fish swim.
